correctness.rationale: Exact integration gives A(h) and A(1)^2=0. A direct polynomial covariance lift gives K(delta^2), det(I-K)=-F(delta^2)/2 and a nonsingular branch commutator for every 0<delta<1. A Brouwer positive eigenmatrix of the adjoint map must be definite; positive-order domination makes its eigenvalue the second-moment spectral radius and produces an exact identity for every deterministic initial state. Continuity, r(0)=0, r(1)=5 and the single root of F on (0,1) prove the exhaustive threshold. An exact rational positive definite P proves the mixed unstable-branch witness. The independent standard-library replay passes 106 exact assertions/finite path checks; the finite tests are not mistaken for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Unit-period two-step deadbeat double-integrator feedback is a natural aggressive sampled-data design. The theorem gives its exact stochastic clock-jitter robustness margin, behavior at the exact boundary, and a strict interval in which one unstable deterministic sampling branch is nevertheless mean-square stabilizable by independent mixing. The rational Lyapunov example makes the consequence practical and independently checkable; no broad optimal design claim is made.
